description: This topic explains the meaning, types and indicators of development, the difference between growth and development, sustainable development and its pillars, developed versus developing countries, obstacles to development in Tanzania and Africa, and the roles of citizens, government and self-reliance, including the Tanzania Development Vision 2025.

mcq.questionText: What is the best meaning of the term development?

options.text: A positive and continuous change that improves people's lives
An increase in the number of buildings only
Buying many imported goods from abroad

mcq.explanation: Development is a positive, continuous process of change that raises people's standard of living and well-being in many areas of life.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of individual or personal development?

options.text: A student completing school and gaining useful skills

mcq.explanation: Individual or personal development concerns improvements in a single person's knowledge, skills, income and well-being, such as completing school.

mcq.questionText: Economic development mainly deals with improvements in which area?

options.text: Production, income and use of resources
The size of a country's flag

mcq.explanation: Economic development focuses on increasing production, income, employment and the efficient use of resources to improve livelihoods.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an indicator used to measure development?

options.text: The age of the national anthem

mcq.explanation: Life expectancy, income per capita, literacy and access to services are common indicators used to measure the level of development.

mcq.questionText: Economic growth differs from development because growth refers mainly to an increase in:

options.text: The quantity of goods and services produced
The quality of people's health and education
The level of freedom and human rights

mcq.explanation: Growth is a quantitative increase in output (such as GDP), while development includes wider improvements in welfare, equity and quality of life.

mcq.questionText: Which one is NOT a pillar of sustainable development?
mcq.explanation: The three pillars of sustainable development are economic, social and environmental. There is no military pillar.

mcq.questionText: Sustainable development means meeting today's needs while:

options.text: Protecting the ability of future generations to meet their needs
Using up all natural resources quickly

mcq.explanation: Sustainable development satisfies present needs without harming the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

mcq.questionText: Which feature is most common in developing countries such as Tanzania?

options.text: Low income per capita and reliance on agriculture
Very high income per capita for everyone

mcq.explanation: Developing countries usually have lower income per capita, depend heavily on agriculture and have limited industrialisation.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a major obstacle to development in Tanzania and Africa?

options.text: Very high literacy in all areas

mcq.explanation: Poverty, ignorance and disease, identified long ago as the three main enemies of development, remain serious obstacles in Tanzania and Africa.

options.text: It diverts public resources away from services and projects
It increases the number of schools built
It improves the quality of public roads
It raises the income of all citizens equally

mcq.explanation: Corruption steals or misuses public funds meant for services and projects, slowing development and increasing inequality.

mcq.questionText: The Tanzania Development Vision 2025 was created to:

options.text: Guide the country towards a middle-income economy with a high quality of life
Ban all foreign trade by the year 2025
Remove primary education from the country
Make Tanzania depend fully on foreign aid

mcq.explanation: Tanzania Development Vision 2025 set goals such as a high quality of life, good governance, a competitive economy and self-reliance, aiming for middle-income status.

mcq.questionText: Which value did the Arusha Declaration emphasise as a path to development?
mcq.explanation: The Arusha Declaration of 1967 promoted self-reliance, hard work and using local resources rather than depending on outside help.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best shows social development?

options.text: Improved access to education, health and clean water
An increase only in the country's army size
A larger number of luxury cars imported

mcq.explanation: Social development is seen in better education, health, clean water and other services that improve people's welfare.

mcq.questionText: What is the role of citizens in bringing development?

options.text: Working hard, paying taxes and participating in development activities
Waiting for the government to do everything

mcq.explanation: Citizens contribute to development by working hard, paying taxes, protecting public property and taking part in community projects.

mcq.questionText: Which strategy can help reduce dependency and promote development in Tanzania?

options.text: Adding value to local resources and building local industries
Relying only on grants from abroad

mcq.explanation: Processing local resources and building domestic industries creates jobs and income, reducing dependency on foreign goods and aid.

fib.questionText: A positive and continuous change that improves the living standards of people is called _____.
fib.explanation: Development is the gradual, positive change that raises people's standard of living and well-being.

fib.questionText: An increase in the quantity of goods and services produced in a country is called economic _____.
fib.explanation: Economic growth is a quantitative rise in output, often measured by GDP, and differs from broader development.

fib.questionText: The three pillars of sustainable development are economic, social and _____.
fib.explanation: Sustainable development rests on the economic, social and environmental pillars working together.

fib.questionText: The ability to read and write among a population is measured by the _____ rate.
fib.explanation: The literacy rate is a key indicator of educational development in a country.

fib.questionText: The average number of years a person is expected to live is called life _____.
fib.explanation: Life expectancy reflects the level of health and welfare in a country and is a common development indicator.

fib.questionText: The total value of goods and services produced in a country divided by its population is the GDP per _____.
fib.explanation: GDP per capita measures average income per person and is used to compare levels of development.

fib.questionText: The 1967 Arusha Declaration promoted the policy of self-_____ as a way to develop Tanzania.
fib.explanation: The Arusha Declaration emphasised self-reliance, using local resources and hard work.

fib.questionText: Countries with high income, advanced industries and good services are called _____ countries.
fib.explanation: Developed countries have high income per capita, strong industries and good social services.

fib.questionText: The national plan that aims to make Tanzania a middle-income country with a high quality of life is the Tanzania Development _____ 2025.
fib.explanation: Tanzania Development Vision 2025 set long-term goals for quality of life, good governance and a strong economy.

fib.questionText: The misuse of public funds for private gain, which slows development, is called _____.
fib.explanation: Corruption diverts resources meant for services and projects, hindering development.

tf.questionText: Development is a positive change that improves people's lives.
tf.explanation: Development is defined as a positive and continuous change that raises living standards.

tf.questionText: Economic growth and development mean exactly the same thing.
tf.explanation: Growth is only a quantitative increase in output, while development includes wider improvements in welfare and equity.

tf.questionText: Life expectancy and literacy rate are indicators of development.
tf.explanation: Both are widely used indicators that reflect the level of health and education in a country.

tf.questionText: Sustainable development ignores the needs of future generations.
tf.explanation: Sustainable development specifically aims to protect the needs of future generations while meeting today's needs.

tf.questionText: Poverty, ignorance and disease are obstacles to development in Tanzania.
tf.explanation: These three were identified as major enemies of development and remain serious obstacles in Tanzania and Africa.

tf.questionText: Corruption helps to speed up national development.
tf.explanation: Corruption diverts public resources away from services and projects, slowing development.

tf.questionText: Developed countries generally have higher income per capita than developing countries.
tf.explanation: A higher income per capita is one of the main features distinguishing developed from developing countries.

tf.questionText: Self-reliance was a key idea in the Arusha Declaration of 1967.
tf.explanation: The Arusha Declaration promoted self-reliance, hard work and the use of local resources.

tf.questionText: Citizens have no role to play in their country's development.
tf.explanation: Citizens contribute by working hard, paying taxes, protecting public property and joining community projects.

tf.questionText: The Tanzania Development Vision 2025 aims to raise the quality of life and build a competitive economy.
tf.explanation: Vision 2025 set goals including a high quality of life, good governance and a strong, competitive economy.

summary.correctAnswer: Development is a positive and continuous change that improves people's living standards and well-being.
summary.explanation: It captures the idea of ongoing positive change in many areas of life.

summary.questionText: State the difference between economic and social development.
summary.correctAnswer: Economic development improves production and income, while social development improves services such as education, health and clean water.
summary.explanation: Economic development concerns the economy, while social development concerns human welfare and services.

summary.correctAnswer: Income or GDP per capita, life expectancy, literacy rate and access to clean water.
summary.explanation: These indicators measure income, health, education and access to basic services.

summary.questionText: Explain the difference between economic growth and development.
summary.correctAnswer: Growth is a quantitative increase in output such as GDP, while development is broader and includes better welfare, equity and quality of life.
summary.explanation: Growth can occur without development if benefits are not shared or welfare does not improve.

summary.questionText: Name the three pillars of sustainable development.
summary.correctAnswer: The economic pillar, the social pillar and the environmental pillar.
summary.explanation: Sustainable development balances these three pillars together.

summary.correctAnswer: Sustainable development meets the needs of the present without harming the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
summary.explanation: It links current needs with the protection of resources for the future.

summary.questionText: List four obstacles to development in Tanzania and Africa.
summary.correctAnswer: Poverty, ignorance, disease and corruption (also poor infrastructure and dependency).
summary.explanation: These challenges reduce resources, skills, health and trust needed for development.

summary.questionText: Give two roles of the government in promoting development.
summary.correctAnswer: Building infrastructure such as roads and schools, and providing services like health, education and security.
summary.explanation: The government creates the conditions and services that enable development.

summary.questionText: State two ways citizens can contribute to development.
summary.correctAnswer: Working hard and paying taxes, and participating in community development projects.
summary.explanation: Active, hardworking and responsible citizens are essential for development.

summary.questionText: What is the main aim of the Tanzania Development Vision 2025?
summary.correctAnswer: To make Tanzania a middle-income country with a high quality of life, good governance and a strong, self-reliant economy.
summary.explanation: Vision 2025 set long-term national development goals for the country.

hoq.questionText: A country reports a rise in GDP, but most citizens still lack clean water, schools and health care. What does this situation best show?

options.text: Economic growth has occurred without real development
The country has achieved full sustainable development
Growth and development always happen together
The country no longer needs any social services

hoq.explanation: An increase in GDP is growth, but if welfare and services do not improve for the people, real development has not taken place.

hoq.questionText: A district clears a large forest to expand farms, earning money now but causing soil erosion and water shortages later. Which pillar of sustainable development is most neglected?
hoq.explanation: Destroying forests for short-term income harms the environment and future resources, so the environmental pillar is neglected.

hoq.questionText: Two villages receive equal funds for a water project. In one, leaders take part of the money for themselves and the project fails; in the other, the money is used well and clean water is provided. What does this comparison best illustrate?

options.text: Corruption and poor leadership can block development even when resources exist
Clean water is not an indicator of development
Development depends only on foreign aid

hoq.explanation: Equal resources gave different results because of corruption and leadership, showing that good governance is essential for development.
